what: does reading the graph before entry actually separate winners from losers? Each closed trade's graph state is reconstructed from the tape AS OF ITS ENTRY (nothing after the entry is visible to the reconstruction, so no hindsight can leak in), then outcomes are graded inside each bucket.

coupling_status.statement: as of 7.1.4 the graph is a DISPLAY, not an input: CHART_INTEL.json is read by the dashboard and by nothing in the selection path. Sleeves select on confidence score, dip depth, geometry verdict, bounce reliability, reach-vs-cost and trend sign. Peaks, floors, ceilings, peak trajectory and cadence phase are drawn but never consulted.

peak_trajectory.why: no meaningful separation between buckets (spread 0.692% over n=1451) — on this evidence the feature does not yet distinguish good entries

trend.why: no meaningful separation between buckets (spread 0.671% over n=1510) — on this evidence the feature does not yet distinguish good entries

cadence_phase.why: no meaningful separation between buckets (spread 0.855% over n=1422) — on this evidence the feature does not yet distinguish good entries

range_position.why: entries taken at HIGH_THIRD averaged +0.793% vs -0.210% at LOW_THIRD (spread 1.003% over n=1510) — reading this before entry would have separated winners from losers

floor_support.why: no meaningful separation between buckets (spread 0.558% over n=1319) — on this evidence the feature does not yet distinguish good entries

ceiling_overhead.why: no meaningful separation between buckets (spread 0.214% over n=1411) — on this evidence the feature does not yet distinguish good entries

next_step: EVIDENCE FOUND: range_position now separate winners from losers and are still not consulted at entry. These are the features to gate on next — with a knob, a kill switch, and an A/B, never silently.
honesty: this audit grades entries the system already took; it cannot say what would have happened on entries it never took. It answers 'did reading the graph help?', not 'is the graph complete?'
